posts.hook: Crypto's biggest heist on record may have just happened, and Binance is footing the bill
posts.caption: binance says a ~$6.3b hack drained its wallets and it will cover all losses, crowdstrike says china-linked hackers used an ai tool to target 200+ organizations in 11 days, reddit is going logged-in only. full digest at sift.yasint.dev (link in bio)

slides.title: TRM Labs pins Binance's ~$6.3B hack on North Korea, mostly drained in ==20 minutes==
slides.desc: Binance pledges to cover all losses, potentially the largest crypto theft ever.

terms.gloss: a firm that traces stolen crypto across blockchains

slides.title: CrowdStrike: China-linked hackers used AI tool ARTEX on 200+ organizations in 11 days
slides.desc: At least nine were compromised, so recon that took weeks now fits in days.

terms.gloss: the AI tool CrowdStrike says the group used

slides.title: An open-weight model turned unshipped Firefox fixes into working exploits for ==$1,000== each
slides.desc: The gap between a public fix and users getting it is now cheap to attack.

terms.gloss: an AI model whose files anyone can download and run

slides.title: Reddit is going logged-in only and says Google's AI Mode ==does not drive traffic==
slides.desc: October search referrals are down over 1 million a week.

slides.title: Anthropic's S-1 names its dependence on Taiwan-made chips as a risk
slides.desc: It says it depends heavily on TSMC and warns of potential disruption.

terms.gloss: the filing a company makes with US regulators before going public
the Taiwan chipmaker Anthropic relies on
